parsed.why: No criminalisation, but 2024 submissions document rape, assault and service barriers; no general protection, no gender recognition, and a sourced note that a mismatched passport could draw a charge. Police-pride cooperation evidence is dated 2013-16.

Court decriminalisation plus a constitutional reading extending sex discrimination to gender identity; no documented trans targeting beyond one assault, but no statutory protection, no gender recognition, and official resistance history. Thin but structurally non-hostile record.

Military government, documented police bribery arrests under the brief ban, reported 'modesty' charges used against gender-nonconforming people, common individual harassment, unregistered LGBTI groups, entrenched opposite-sex marriage, and active demands to re-criminalise.

Decriminalisation affirmed and now statutory, court-ordered trans gender recognition and LGBT organisation registration actually operating, employment protection on sexual orientation. Offsets: Section 167 unrepealed, no administrative process, unsatisfactory implementation, only moderate tolerance data.

Stable 2022 decriminalisation, but zero discrimination or hate-speech protection, no gender recognition, no union recognition, LGBTQ people avoiding law enforcement (no recourse), and documented official exclusion posture at a port plus government 'no mandate' stance.
